document.title: Let Deck Apps call linked computers through built-in and custom plugins
document.summary: Adds Host Control: a typed SDK client and plugin contract, the `vitadeck-host-companion` CLI, and a native LAN Listener that replaces the upload server and stores links. Two more stories ship with it: long-polling host events with fetch cancel, and new agent skill text.
document.why: [A Deck App had no way to reach the computer next to it.](source:s-pr)

sources.label: PR #144
sources.title: feat(host-control): let Deck Apps call linked computers through built-in and custom plugins
sources.gist: Adds Host Control end to end, then plugins, standalone plugins, events, an always-on LAN Listener and relink. Lists its deviations from the issues.

sources.title: Host Control slice A: wire contract and SDK client
sources.gist: JSON wire contract, typed registry, a client that never rejects, shared fixtures.

sources.title: Host Control slice B: Host Companion CLI
sources.gist: `start` and `link`, a port that never falls forward, a peer check once linked, no computer-acting commands.

sources.title: Host Control slice C: native link listener and Shell Host Control screen
sources.gist: A link listener that runs only on the Host Control screen, a persisted link store, shared HTTP parsing, a no-confirm forget.

sources.label: PR #145
sources.title: feat(host-control): Deck Apps ship their own host plugin as a .vdplugin package
sources.gist: Built-in plugins first, a `.vdplugin` package for a Deck App's own plugin, and two CLIs, one per machine role. Merged into this branch.

sources.label: chatgpt-codex-connector on PR #144
sources.author: chatgpt-codex-connector
sources.body:
**Reject unauthorized peers before reading their bodies**

When a non-linked LAN peer sends a slow or concurrent request, `reply` waits for `readBody` to finish before checking `isAllowed`; `readBody` continues consuming the stream and buffers up to 64 KiB per request, so denied peers can tie up sockets and memory before receiving a 403. Check the peer before reading the body, or abort unauthorized requests immediately, so the allowlist also protects availability.

sources.label: matemolnar8 on PR #144
sources.author: matemolnar8
sources.body:
> [!NOTE]
> 🤖 **Claude Opus 5.5 responding on behalf of Máté Molnár**

Fixed in 04760101. `reply` now runs `isAllowed` before `readBody`. A peer that is not linked gets the 403 straight away, and `request.resume()` discards its body without buffering it. The peer-check tests in `test/server.test.ts` still pass (24/24).

lookFor: [#111](source:s-111) asks for a separate link listener on port 8798 that runs only while the Host Control screen is open. Head has one always-on listener on 8787 for uploads and links. [The body](source:s-pr) gives the reason: setup felt clunky after testing.

[#111](source:s-111) asks for `nativeGetHostControlUrl(): string` and one stored link. Head exposes `nativeGetHostControlLinks` and keeps several links in `host-control-links.json`. [The body](source:s-pr) lists this as a deviation.

[#109](source:s-109) keeps `defineHostCommands` internal because the companion is VitaDeck-owned, and it sends no `plugin` field. Head lets authors define plugins with `defineHostPlugin`, and the wire request gains `plugin`. [The body](source:s-pr) and [#145](source:s-145) give the reason.

[#110](source:s-110) has the companion run from source through tsx and store one `vita`. Head bundles it with a `vitadeck-host-companion` bin and stores a `vitas` list. [#145](source:s-145) says the pnpm-only CLI was clunky for users, and [the body](source:s-pr) lists several links as a deviation.

[The body](source:s-pr) says credentials are deferred, "so only read-only built-ins exist". The same body lists `core.notify`, which sends a notice to every watching Deck App, and `server.ts` runs it for any allowed peer. It writes to the companion's event log and does not act on the computer.

[The body](source:s-pr) says `watchHostEvents` means no events "fall between two waits". It also says the companion keeps only 100 events per plugin, and its ledger declines exact restart detection. A gap past 100 events, or a missed restart, cannot be replayed.
[The body](source:s-pr) opens its review section with "Three review loops ran, one per request". Its table lists six: Host Control, Plugin UX, Standalone plugins, Events, LAN Listener and Relink.

[The body's Cursor summary](source:s-pr) says "Reviewed by Cursor Bugbot for commit ae5083ca". All 17 of Cursor's conversation comments [say Bugbot could not run](source:c-bugbot) because of a usage limit. The summary is not evidence of a Bugbot review.

[Cursor's approval agent](source:c-cursor) says human review is needed and no reviewers were assigned. All 19 GitHub reviews have the state COMMENTED: 17 from Cursor, one from Codex and one author reply. The PR records no GitHub approval, and the review table in the body lists only AI reviewers.

parts.name: Host Control
parts.summary: Link a computer once, then call typed commands on it from a Deck App, through built-in or custom plugins.

parts.name: Host events
parts.summary: Plugins push events to Deck Apps through a held `core.events` request, and native `fetch` cancels on Deck App stop so a held wait never stalls a reload.

groups.title: Wire contract, plugin types and SDK client
groups.why: Every other group builds on this contract. [#109](source:s-109) asks for JSON over HTTP, shared fixtures and methods that never reject. [The body](source:s-pr) turns the flat command list into plugins.
groups.summary: `protocol.ts` and `plugin.ts` define what `client.ts` sends, and the fixtures in `tests/fixtures/host-control/` pin those bytes for the SDK, companion and C tests.

attention.note: `createHostClient(plugin)` without `hostId` calls `linkedHosts()[0]`, read at each call. Link computer A, then B, and every default client moves to B on its next call, with no signal to the Deck App. A relink edits in place (`link.c:199`) and does not reorder, so decide whether "most recently linked" is a promise authors can rely on.

notes.body: A success body is cast, not checked. The registry's guards cover payloads only, so `ResultOf<C>` is a compile-time promise that a different companion version can break.

groups.title: Companion command server, peer check and built-ins
groups.why: [#110](source:s-110) asks for a companion that serves `POST /command` and answers only the linked Vita once linked. [Codex asked](source:c-codex) that the peer check run before the body is read.
groups.summary: `server.ts` answers an unlinked peer with [a 403 and discards its body unbuffered](source:c-mate), then checks the request and the plugin's payload guard before it runs a command from `core.ts` or `system-stats.ts`.

attention.note: `isAllowed` returns true for every peer when `vitas` is empty. A companion that was never linked answers the whole LAN on `0.0.0.0`, and so does one whose last Vita was forgotten, because relink empties `vitas`. Installed plugins are then callable too, so decide whether an empty list should mean open or loopback-only.

notes.body: Only the peer check moved ahead of `readBody`. An allowed peer's body is still read before the route, method and content type checks.
`ok` spreads last so a plugin's result cannot claim success on its own. This is finding R2 in the body's ledger.

groups.title: One always-on LAN Listener replaces the upload server
groups.why: [The body](source:s-pr) says linking only from the Host Control screen felt clunky in testing, so links share an always-on listener with Runtime Upload. [#111](source:s-111) asks for the shared parsing in `src/net/`.
groups.summary: `lan_listener.c` takes over the upload routes from the deleted `http_server.c` and adds `POST /link`, using request parsing moved to `net/http.c` and an address from `src/platform/lan_address_*`.

attention.note: [The body](source:s-pr) accepts that anyone on the LAN can upload a Deck App or add a link whenever VitaDeck runs. `POST /link` with any valid `id` and `url` puts that link first, so a default `createHostClient` then sends its commands there. Turning the listener off lasts only until the next launch, so decide whether always-on without credentials is the right default on a shared network.

notes.body: The ingest lock is taken before the body is read. A slow uploader makes every other upload answer 409 until it finishes or goes quiet for 15 s.
With every client slot in use, a new connection closes with no reply. Now that the listener is always on, any LAN peer can occupy those slots for 15 s per read.
The port falls forward through 8796 when 8787 is busy. #110 rejects fall-forward for the companion because a stored URL would break.

groups.title: Companion `link` and relink on start
groups.why: [The body](source:s-pr) wants a new computer IP or port to reach the Vita without running `link` again. [A later commit](source:k-relink-queue) runs attempts one at a time because each one rewrites the config.
groups.summary: `start` in `cli.ts` passes every saved Vita to `relink`, which calls `linkVita` from `link.ts` through one queue and retries every 30 s while a Vita does not answer.
questions: Why does the relink loop target port 8787 when `lan_listener_start` can fall forward as far as 8796?

notes.body: Only an outcome with `retry` schedules another attempt. A thrown error logs once and that Vita gets no more retries until the next `start`.

groups.why: [#111](source:s-111) asks for a Host Control screen that lists links. An always-on listener also needs an off switch, and [an empty Shell must not put the first Cross on it](source:k-empty-shell).

focus.caption: Cross forgets with no confirm, unlike package removal; #111 chose that because relinking is cheap. Check the focus move when the last row goes.

groups.title: Companion loads, installs and hot-reloads `.vdplugin` packages
groups.why: [#145](source:s-145) says a custom plugin meant an npm package of its own, and a globally installed companion could not load one installed somewhere else.
groups.summary: `install` in `cli.ts` stages a package with `extractHostPluginArchive`, proves it with `loadHostPluginPackage` and renames it into place, and `start` reloads it through `setPlugins` when files change.

attention.note: A package runs with the user's permissions, and nothing limits what its commands do. [#145](source:s-145) holds back computer-acting built-ins for the credentials decision, yet an installed custom plugin can act on the computer for any allowed peer today. Decide whether the warning in the `install` usage text is enough until credentials exist.

questions: Why does `install` import the package's entry to learn its plugin id, when the manifest could carry that id?

notes.body: `install` imports the entry here, so the package's top-level code runs before the built-in id check on the next line.
The content hash busts Node's module cache, and old versions stay in it. A long `--plugin` session grows by one module per rebuild.

groups.title: Host events by long-polling
groups.why: [The body](source:s-pr) wants plugins to push events to Deck Apps the moment something happens on the computer, and it says ADR 0004 rejects WebSocket, SSE and a Vita listener. [Lifecycles start only after the port binds](source:k-lifecycle), so a busy port leaves no plugin timer running.
groups.summary: A plugin's `start(emit)` lifecycle feeds `events.ts`, `core.events` holds a request on that log for up to 25 s, and `watchHostEvents` keeps one such request open.

notes.body: Watching any plugin goes through the `core` plugin's `events` command, so a custom plugin needs no event route of its own.
The `running` flag belongs to one `startPlugins` call, so a stopped plugin's late emit is dropped even after a reload.

fileNotes.js/packages/host-companion/src/events.ts: `createEventLog`: waiters and the per-plugin event window.
fileNotes.js/packages/host-companion/src/server.ts: `startPlugins` runs lifecycles and drops emits after a stop.
fileNotes.js/packages/host-companion/test/server.t: Also covers held waits, restarts and dropped emits.
fileNotes.js/packages/sdk/test/host-control.test.t: Also covers `after` handling and stopping from a callback.

groups.title: Native fetch cancels when a Deck App stops
groups.why: A held event wait must not stall a reload. [The body](source:s-pr) measures 15 s before the fix and under 3 s after.
groups.summary: `fetch_shutdown` marks every pending request cancelled, and the new curl progress callback in `fetch.c` aborts each transfer, which `js_limits_harness` proves with a server that never answers.

attention.note: This applies to every fetch of every Deck App, not only event waits. A Deck App that sends a `POST` and then stops used to wait in `fetch_shutdown` until the transfer finished. Now that transfer aborts at curl's next progress call and the request may not complete, so decide whether a reload may drop in-flight writes.

notes.body: Every curl progress call of every fetch now takes the shared `fetch_mutex`, which is the cost of checking one flag.

fileNotes.src/jslib/fetch.c: Adds `cancelled`, the progress callback and the shutdown loop.
fileNotes.tests/js_limits_harness.c: Stops a Deck App while its fetch waits on a silent server.

[The body](source:s-pr) adds standalone plugins that any Deck App can depend on, [with the SDK as a peer dependency](source:k-peer-sdk). [A broken build keeps the last good package](source:k-broken-build) so the running companion is not left without it.
groups.summary: `resolveHostPlugin` and `buildHostPlugin` in `cli.ts` turn `hostPlugin` in `vitadeck.config.json` into the `.vdplugin` package and zip the companion loads, and the templates scaffold that config.

groups.title: Host Control demo Deck App
groups.why: [The body](source:s-pr) uses this Deck App for its manual passes: every linked computer with live CPU, and capabilities, gauges and an Echo round trip for the selected one.
groups.summary: `App.tsx` reads `linkedHosts`, polls `systemStats` for each host and shows `HostDetails` for the selected one, with the other files making it a buildable example.

groups.title: ADR, glossary and author docs
groups.why: [The body](source:s-pr) rewrites ADR 0004, `CONTEXT.md`, `AGENTS.md` and the READMEs in place, with new terms such as **Host Control Plugin** and **LAN Listener**.
groups.summary: These files carry the design decisions and author-facing commands of the groups above; ADR 0004 is the one that records the always-on listener and the deferred credentials.

groups.title: Host events by long-polling
groups.why: [The body](source:s-pr) wants plugins to push events to Deck Apps the moment something happens on the computer, and it says ADR 0004 rejects WebSocket, SSE and a Vita listener. [Lifecycles start only after the port binds](source:k-lifecycle), so a busy port leaves no plugin timer running.
groups.summary: A plugin's `start(emit)` lifecycle feeds `events.ts`, `core.events` holds a request on that log for up to 25 s, and `watchHostEvents` keeps one such request open.

groups.title: Native fetch cancels when a Deck App stops
groups.why: A held event wait must not stall a reload. [The body](source:s-pr) measures 15 s before the fix and under 3 s after.
groups.summary: `fetch_shutdown` marks every pending request cancelled, and the new curl progress callback in `fetch.c` aborts each transfer, which `js_limits_harness` proves with a server that never answers.

attention.note: This applies to every fetch of every Deck App, not only event waits. A Deck App that sends a `POST` and then stops used to wait in `fetch_shutdown` until the transfer finished. Now that transfer aborts at curl's next progress call and the request may not complete, so decide whether a reload may drop in-flight writes.

groups.title: Agent skills for Host Control
groups.why: [The body](source:s-pr) adds a public `vitadeck-host-control` skill and extends the skills that scaffold, test and upload, so agents can use the feature. The code works without this text, so it could have been its own PR.
groups.summary: The new skill covers the companion, linking, plugin authoring and error codes, and the other skills gain short pointers to it and to the new build outputs.

commits.subject: fix(host-companion): relink attempts run one at a time and re-read the config
commits.author: Máté Molnár
commits.body:
Retries for different Vitas ran on independent timers, and each save
wrote the same temporary file from a config read before the request.
All attempts now share one queue, a failure is logged, and linkVita
reads the config again just before changing its Vitas. Also list
unknown_link with the other link endpoint codes.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commits.subject: feat(host-control): the companion relinks its Vitas on every start
commits.author: Máté Molnár
commits.body:
A new computer IP or companion port broke commands until the user ran
`link` again. `start` now re-sends the link to every Vita in its config
with `relink: true`, which VitaDeck applies only to a link it still has,
so a computer forgotten in the Shell is not linked back: VitaDeck
answers 404 `unknown_link` and the companion drops that Vita. A Vita
that does not answer is retried every 30 s. The host-control demo asks
for capabilities again when a relink changes the URL.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

A busy port no longer leaves a plugin's timers running. Stopping twice is a

commits.subject: feat(host-control): computers push events to Deck Apps by long-polling
commits.author: Máté Molnár
commits.body:
A plugin declares Host Control Events next to its commands and emits them
from a start(emit) lifecycle the companion runs while it is loaded. The
companion numbers recent events, and core.events holds a request until the
plugin's next event or 25 s. watchHostEvents in the SDK keeps one such
request open, so an event reaches the Vita within one round trip. core.notify
and `vitadeck-host-companion notify` let any script send a notice, which the
host-control demo shows.

Stopping a Deck App now cancels its pending fetches through curl's progress
callback, so a held request no longer stalls a reload or shutdown.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commits.author: Máté Molnár
commits.body:
A vitadeck.config.json may have hostPlugin without an entry: build then
writes only the .vdplugin package and zip, and dev rebuilds them without a
Runtime Upload URL. `vitadeck create <name> --host-plugin-only` scaffolds such
a project, whose package.json exports host/plugin.ts so any Deck App can
depend on it. Template package.json files all get published versions.

Bundle before replacing the package folder, copy linked files as files, and

commits.subject: feat(host-control): a Deck App's plugin ships as a .vdplugin package and zip
commits.author: Máté Molnár
commits.body:
Plugins will carry more than code (scripts, data, binaries), so the single
bundled file becomes a package like the Deck App's: `vitadeck build` writes a
<slug>.vdplugin folder (manifest.json, companion.mjs, optional files/) and a
<slug>.vdplugin.zip. `hostPlugin` becomes { entry, files? }. The companion
installs archives or folders into ~/.vitadeck/plugins/<id>.vdplugin, loads the
entry by file URL so it finds its files through import.meta.url, and watches
package folders recursively.

commits.subject: fix(host-companion): load plugins from file copies, resolve paths from the cwd
commits.author: Máté Molnár
commits.body:
A bundled CommonJS dependency calls createRequire(import.meta.url), which a
data: URL cannot satisfy; plugins now load from a content-hashed .mjs copy.
Paths resolve against the working directory except under the repo's own
`host-companion` script, so a Deck App's `host` script works from anywhere.
Plugin ids may start with a digit, and watcher errors are logged.

commits.subject: feat(host-control): built-in plugins, .vdplugin files, vitadeck-host-companion
commits.author: Máté Molnár
commits.body:
A Deck App now keeps its own Host Control Plugin in its project: `hostPlugin`
in vitadeck.config.json makes `vitadeck build` bundle the implementation into
one self-contained <slug>.vdplugin, and `vitadeck create --host-plugin`
scaffolds it. Users install that file with `vitadeck-host-companion install`;
the companion reloads installed and --plugin files when they change.

systemStats moves into the companion as a built-in, with its registry in
@vitadeck/sdk/host-control next to implementHostPlugin and HostCommandError.
The companion is a dependency-free bundled package with the
vitadeck-host-companion bin, and js/host-plugins is gone.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commits.subject: feat(host-control): Host Control Link listener, store, getter, and Shell screen
commits.author: Máté Molnár
commits.body:
Slice C of ADR 0004. VitaDeck keeps up to four Host Control Links in <data root>/host-control-links.json and exposes them to Deck Apps through nativeGetHostControlLinks. The Shell Host Control Screen starts a listener on 8798-8807 that accepts one POST /link, and Cross forgets a linked computer.

Upload's HTTP helpers move to src/net/http, LAN address detection to src/platform/lan_address_*, jimp's implementation and the JSON skip and escape helpers to src/core/json, and Deck App Storage's Vita-safe file replace to src/core/util so the link store reuses it.
